test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: There is 70% increase in an amount in 7 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on ₹8,000 after 3 years at the same rate of interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Amount increased by 70% in 7 years

For compound interest sum = Rs. 8000

Time = 3 years

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

C.I = [P(1 + R/100)T - 1]

Here, P = sum, T = time, R = rate

**Calculation:**

Let the amount be Rs. 100a

So, increased amount = 100a + 100a × 70%

⇒ 170a

So, interest = 170a - 100a = 70a

Now, Let the rate of the interest be R

70a = (100a × 7 × R)/100

⇒ 7aR = 70a

⇒ R = 10

So, rate = 10%

Now, C.I = 8000[(1 + 10/100)³ - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1 + 1/10)3 - 1]

⇒ 8000[(11/10)3 - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1331/1000) - 1]

⇒ 8000[(1331 - 1000)/1000]

⇒ 8000[331/1000]

⇒ 8 × 331 = 2648

**∴ The compound interest is Rs. 2648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Simple interest is constant throughout the period.

So, 70% in 7 years = 10 % in 1 year

∴ R = 10% and T = 3 years

Let the sum be 10 units, So, Amount = 10 + 10/100 = 11

For three years , sum = 10³ = 1000

1000 units = Rs. 8000, therefore 1 unit = Rs. 8

And Amount = 11³ = 1331

Interest = 1331 - 1000 = 331

Interest = 331 × 8 = 2648.

∴ The compound interest is Rs. 2648.
